report:
PASS for the exact retained PARTIAL mathematical scope. The argument establishes actual realization, uniqueness modulo constants, and I-convergence of every normalized actual E1 maximizing sequence on cones admitting one smooth rational projective quotient for the specified torus. The universal topology, orbit-pushforward and conditional root-L1 assertions also hold on their stated domains. This verdict does not complete original P13.2 or certify native publication.

The accepted P13.1 and round73 mathematical bodies are used only within their explicitly granted scope. In particular, actual classes, raw order-preserving root bijections, fixed-field products, calibrated continuous rational correspondence, weighted decreasing-net continuity, finite-target integrability, midpoint bounds and outer differentiation are available. Neither general compactness nor inverse existence is inherited from those grants. Unreviewed drafts and documentary observations supply no mathematical premises.

For n1, the supremum tests are finite on normalized actual PSH. Genuine decreasing CPSH majorants separate distinct restrictions. The energy infimum over continuous majorants proves upper semicontinuity directly: S_psi(v)<epsilon implies v<=psi+epsilon. The root threshold identity uses the actual inverse root of psi+t, which is a permissible CPSH test even when it is not normalized. Strict inequalities require uniform gaps, not merely pointwise order. A downward source shift c produces a downward target gap at least c/b; the inverse produces a gap at least ac. These bounds establish both strict sublevel and strict superlevel continuity. The resulting homeomorphism asserts no strong-I continuity or universal compactness.

For n2, T_r is a continuous self-map of the actual carrier. Orbit slopes and equivariance give |u(T_r x)-u(x)|<=2b|r| wherever u is finite, and preserve its minus-infinity locus. Consequently its Radon pushforward integrates every actual source E1 potential. The granted integrability criterion establishes finite dual energy; no MA pullback identity is needed.

The root-L1 lemma is correct for arbitrary nets. For each fixed index, integrability excludes the exceptional loci of the two potentials being compared; finite orbit slopes then control their entire finite orbits. No common null set for an uncountable net is required. With a fixed rational M and finite rational grid, the clipped-root estimate is bounded by a^(-1) times the sum of finitely many orbit-sample L1 errors, plus 2bh/a. Boundary clipping follows from the same minimum-slope inequality. The net limit is taken with that grid fixed, followed by mesh refinement. The tail inequality is |R_i-max(R_i,-M)|<=a^(-1)(-u_i-aM)_+. Source L1 convergence controls these tails at each fixed M, giving limsup ||R_i-R||_1<=2a^(-1) integral(-u-aM)_+. The cutoff tends to infinity last. Thus the lemma retains exactly its stated L1 antecedents and makes no moving-MA assertion.

I checked the pertinent projective statements and proof bodies in [Boucksom–Jonsson v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4). The smooth envelope theorem applies to the actual integral, connected, smooth projective Y over the retained field and its ample L_d. Its multiplier-ideal proof supplies uniform envelope approximation on smooth test models. Normalized compactness then follows through bounded divisorial values, Tychonoff and decreasing upper-tail envelopes. Neither argument requires a countable field or metrizability. The ample-class regularization statements genuinely permit sections of powers of the original L_d; they do not replace its line-bundle reference by another numerical representative.

Torification preserves that reference. Splitting globally generating sections into residual weight components, with their original coefficients, preserves global generation and produces phi composed with q, dominating phi. Uniform approximation and genuine decreasing nets extend this to CPSH and PSH. The trivial valuation remains fixed, and energy monotonicity preserves actual E1. In both directions, the unbounded rational correspondence is obtained from actual decreasing CPSH nets with a nontrivial value at the trivial valuation. Decreasing energy continuity consequently extends the calibration, including energy minus infinity.

The factors remain V_eta=s^(-n)d^(1-n)(L_d^p), omega_eta=L_d/(sd), omega_eta^p=sV_eta and E_eta=E_Ld/(sd). Projective mixed probabilities divide raw curvature by (L_d^p), not by V_eta. The bounded calibrated identities extend at this one fixed rational field through weighted decreasing nets. The limiting weight is integrable because it is E1. Support persists in the closed carrier B, so the lift through ell remains defined, preserves probability mass, and gives exactly the claimed weighted identity with factor 1/(sd).

The compactness argument avoids an unproved closure assertion for invariant potentials. The map A from the genuine compact normalized projective class is an actual surjection. For invariant Psi, sup_Y(phi composed with q-Psi)=sup_B(phi-Psi)=sup_Y(phi-Psi): restriction to B gives one inequality, and torification domination gives the other. Proposition 4.28 therefore makes A continuous for the supremum-test topology. Its Hausdorff target is compact.

The supported projective lift of a finite-energy cone probability is genuinely finite energy. Every projective E1 potential torifies to E1 and agrees with its torification on B; actual cone integrability therefore gives projective integrability, and Theorem 9.20 applies. For bounded-J cone nets, any alleged L1 failure admits a projectively convergent subnet. Energy upper semicontinuity makes its limit E1, continuity of A identifies its carrier restriction, and Proposition 9.19 contradicts the failure. This proves convergence of the whole original net. The source's signed-integration proof uses uniform approximation by model-MA pairings supported at finitely many divisorial points. Absolute L1 follows from the corrected maximum identity and bounded energy of normalized maxima, rather than from signed convergence alone.

Root homeomorphisms transfer actual compactness to every fixed xi. The inverse-root energy comparison bounds J at eta; the orbit pushforwards supply every required finite-energy target, and the finite-grid lemma transfers their L1 convergence back to xi. No unbounded currents are transported across varying Reeb fields.

For n3, the deficit bound gives J(w_j)<=(L+d_j)/(2a_p). A compact subnet has an actual PSH limit, upper semicontinuity makes its energy finite, and target L1 continuity makes the variational objective upper semicontinuous. The actual E1 dual-supremum equality supplies the opposite inequality, proving attainment. Applying the outer obstacle inequality to w+tf and using both signs of differentiation forces equality of MA and target integrals on the dense continuous direction lattice. Both measures are genuine probabilities on K, so MA_xi(w)=mu. The granted tangent identity proves necessity, and the existing embedding proves uniqueness modulo constants.

The whole-sequence claim also holds beyond the particular FS sequence chosen for attainment. For any normalized actual E1 maximizing sequence, the midpoint inequality against the attained maximizer gives I(w_j,w)<=d_j/(2a_p). The granted signed target estimate then identifies target-integral limits, and the maximizing identity identifies energy limits. No I-completeness assumption is used. For p=1, a_1=1/16 and I<=8d. For n=1, the granted effective normal grading gives k[z], the one-point carrier, E(c)=c and the calibrated radial Dirac probability; no estimate involving a_0 is applied.

The dimension-two assertion is valid. Normal integral projective curve quotients have one-dimensional Noetherian normal closed local rings, hence DVRs and regular local rings. Over the perfect retained field, regularity implies smoothness. I checked these implications in [Stacks 00PD](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00PD) and [Stacks 0B8X](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B8X).

The scalar quadric example is correct. Its invariant-ring presentation proves normality as an ungraded ring; it need not identify the covering polynomial ring's grading with the specified ordinary scalar grading. The latter grading gives a good three-dimensional cone. Its projective quotient has local equation uv=w^2, local dimension two and cotangent dimension three at the stated vertex. Every rational Reeb in the specified one-dimensional torus gives the same singular Proj. This establishes failure of the additional hypothesis, not nonexistence of MA solutions.

Harmless printing corrections are explicit: the absolute-value identity is 2max(a,b)-a-b; weighted integration is the test-containing pairing minus the zero-test pairing. In checking the source dependencies, the difference-of-powers telescope includes j=0 through p-1, and the quadratic scaling factor is t[1-(1-t)^p], bounded by pt^2. These corrections follow directly from the displayed algebra and source proof expansions. The p=1 case uses direct quadratic Cauchy–Schwarz. They require no substantive repair of the round79 argument.

The n4 gap analysis is sound. On cones without a smooth rational quotient, this packet still supplies no unconditional actual compactness or realization theorem. Its proposed extension remains conditional on independently established bounded-energy compactness and finite-energy-target L1 continuity at a normal rational quotient. The projective completeness equivalence does not establish that antecedent. No general singular EP, invariant-subset closure, all-point weak convergence or actual realization on all higher-dimensional singular quotients has been assumed.

passages.statement: Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Example 3.9, Theorems 4.5 and 4.15, Corollary 4.16 and Definition 4.20: for an integral projective variety Y over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample line bundle L, PSH(c1(L)) consists of nontrivial pointwise decreasing-net limits of Fubini–Study potentials from powers of this same L with its trivial reference. Continuous PSH potentials are their uniform closure; nontrivial decreasing PSH limits remain PSH. Divisorial values determine these potentials, and their weak topology is pointwise convergence on divisorial valuations.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Proposition 4.28: for an integral projective variety Y over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, an ample line bundle L and any continuous real function gamma on Y^an, phi maps to sup_Y^an(phi-gamma) continuously on PSH(L) with its weak divisorial topology.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorems 5.11 and 5.20 and Corollary 5.21: if Y is smooth and connected over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and L is ample, the class c1(L) has the envelope property and the actual normalized class {phi in PSH(L): sup phi=0} is weakly compact, without a countability hypothesis on the field.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 7.1 and Proposition 7.7: for an integral projective variety Y of dimension p over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample L, the normalized projective energy E_L(phi)=(L,phi)^(p+1)/((p+1)(L^p)) extends to actual PSH by the infimum over dominating continuous PSH potentials. It is increasing, concave, weakly upper semicontinuous, satisfies E_L(phi+c)=E_L(phi)+c, and is continuous along decreasing nets, including energy minus infinity.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Propositions 7.18, 7.19 and 7.21: on an integral projective Y of dimension p>=1 over an algebraically closed trivially valued field with ample L, actual E1(L) potentials define positive Radon mixed curvature measures of raw mass (L^p); every E1(L) potential is integrable against these measures. Model mixed measures have finite divisorial support. Joint decreasing nets with actual E1 limits give weak convergence of both mixed measures and their E1-weighted measures. More generally, the weighted assertion for a limiting PSH weight requires its integrability against the limiting mixed measure.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Propositions 7.18, 7.19 and 7.21: on an integral projective Y of dimension p>=1 over an algebraically closed trivially valued field with ample L, actual E1(L) potentials define positive Radon mixed curvature measures of raw mass (L^p); every E1(L) potential is integrable against these measures. Model mixed measures have finite divisorial support. Joint decreasing nets with actual E1 limits give weak convergence of both mixed measures and their E1-weighted measures. More generally, the weighted assertion for a limiting PSH weight requires its integrability against the limiting mixed measure.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Proposition 9.19: on an integral projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field with ample L, if phi_i converges weakly to phi in actual PSH(L) and J_L(phi_i) is eventually bounded, then phi is E1 and phi_i converges to phi in L1(lambda) for every Radon probability lambda of finite projective dual energy.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 9.20: for an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and ample L, a Radon probability lambda has finite projective dual energy if and only if every actual E1(L) potential belongs to L1(lambda).

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 12.8: for an integral projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample class omega, the envelope property for omega, surjectivity of the actual MA operator from E1(omega) onto finite-dual-energy Radon probabilities, and completeness of E1(omega)/R for its I_omega quasimetric are equivalent.
A Noetherian local normal domain of dimension one is a discrete valuation ring and a regular local ring of dimension one; these conditions are equivalent. Stacks Project, Lemma 10.119.7, tag 00PD.
passages.quote: The ring $A$ is a Noetherian local normal domain of dimension $1$.

passages.statement: For a reduced finite-type scheme X over a perfect field k, X is smooth over k at a point x if and only if its local ring O_X,x is regular. Stacks Project, Lemma 33.25.8, tag 0B8X.
